screens_reviewed: Single scroll capture of audit step 1 (Context) on iPad in the dark-theme screenshot set: native stack header, step chip + progress card, 9-step pill nav, and the 'Visit details' card with read-only fields and single-column choice questions; footer with Back / Save & exit / Next.
verdict: The wizard is on-brand and uses the responsive content container so cards are centered with gutters rather than stretched edge-to-edge, which is the right instinct for iPad. But two real problems dominate: the screen renders the static light palette even in the dark set (it never calls useDesignSystem), and the form content uses the wide contentMaxWidth (~1040–1200) instead of formMaxWidth (600), so a single column of radio options runs the full tablet width with large dead space. As an iPad layout it is a centered, scaled-up phone form rather than one adapted to the canvas.

critical_issues.issue: The screen imports the static `designSystem` (light-only) and reads `designSystem.colors`/`designSystem.fonts` throughout instead of subscribing to `useDesignSystem()`. The static export is hard-wired to `lightColors` (background #FBFAF6, surface #FFFFFF), so in the dark-theme run the audit step still renders the cream/light palette. This matches the screenshot, which is in the 'dark' set yet shows a light background and a near-black selected option pill — i.e. the auditor's dark preference is silently dropped on this whole flow.
critical_issues.evidence: step.tsx:23 `import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system"` (static, not the hook); design-system.ts:453-460 `export const designSystem = { colors: lightColors, ... }`; design-system.ts:501-510 `useDesignSystem()` is the theme-aware hook that this screen never calls; screenshot shows light surfaces in the dark capture.
critical_issues.fix: Replace the module-level `designSystem` usage with `const designSystem = useDesignSystem();` inside `AuditStepScreen` and thread the resolved tokens (or the colors object) down to StepHeader/Card/OptionGrid/FooterNav etc., mirroring how YeeStackHeaderTitle.tsx:1914 already does it. Sub-components that currently read the static import must receive the theme-aware colors via props or their own hook call.

critical_issues.issue: The scroll container is built with `getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, { bottomPadding, gap })` with no `maxWidth` override, so it falls back to `contentMaxWidth` (1040 narrow tablet → 1200 wide, per responsive-layout-tokens.ts:779-780). This is a single-column survey form, and the design system already defines `formMaxWidth = 600` (NARROW/WIDE_TABLET_FORM_MAX_WIDTH) exactly for this case. The result on iPad is a ~1000px-wide column of short radio options ('Yes', 'No', 'Once or twice a week') with large empty trailing space, hurting readability and scan length.
critical_issues.evidence: step.tsx:434-437 omits `maxWidth`; responsive-layout-tokens.ts:973 `formMaxWidth: isTablet ? NARROW_TABLET_FORM_MAX_WIDTH : ...` (600); responsive-layout-tokens.ts:782-783 form widths; screenshot shows full-width option rows on iPad.
critical_issues.fix: Pass `maxWidth: layout.formMaxWidth` into `getResponsiveContentContainerStyle` so the survey column is constrained to ~600 on iPad, matching the design system's form track. Keep the existing gutters/centering behavior.

improvements.issue: OptionGrid is named a grid but renders a single vertical YStack of full-width buttons at every breakpoint. On iPad this wastes the wide canvas: short option sets (Yes/No/Not sure; season; weather) could lay out as a 2-up wrapping row.
improvements.suggestion: When `layout.isTablet`, render options in a wrapping XStack (flexWrap) with each SelectionButton at ~`flexBasis: '48%'` / min-width, so short-label questions form two columns and long-label questions still wrap to full width.
improvements.evidence: step.tsx:1256 `<YStack gap="$2">` is the only layout; no `layout`/`isTablet` branch in OptionGrid.

improvements.issue: FooterNav uses `horizontalPadding={layout.screenPaddingHorizontal}` (28–36 on tablet), so the absolutely-positioned footer spans edge-to-edge while the scroll content is centered in a ~600–1040 track. On iPad the Back/Save & exit/Next buttons stretch far wider than the form above them.
improvements.suggestion: Constrain the footer inner row to the same centered track (e.g. wrap the XStack in a maxWidth/alignSelf:center container matching the content/form width) so the primary CTA group lines up with the form and the Next button stays in comfortable reach.
improvements.evidence: step.tsx:483 passes screenPaddingHorizontal; FooterNav style only sets paddingHorizontal, no maxWidth; screenshot footer is full-width.

improvements.issue: Body and label font sizes are hard-coded (StepHeader title 30, Card title 22, QuestionCard 16, eyebrow 11) and the screen never applies `fontScale` or the tablet typography base scale the design system defines for iPad legibility.
improvements.suggestion: Once the screen adopts useDesignSystem, multiply key sizes by `designSystem.fontScale` (and consider TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE from responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792) so iPad text scales up as intended rather than rendering at phone sizes.
improvements.evidence: responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792 TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3; step.tsx:614 fontSize={30}, :1094 fontSize={22}, :1168 fontSize={16} are literals with no scale.

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used is (none): the screen hand-rolls every surface (Card, QuestionCard, SelectionButton, NoticeCard, SectionProgressCard) from raw YStack/XStack with inline `style` objects and the static `designSystem` tokens instead of the shared ui/* primitives (e.g. Badge.tsx exists in core for the chip/eyebrow treatment). step.tsx:1551-1563 shows Badge is available but the StepHeader 'Step X of 9' / progress chip are built inline (step.tsx:592-608, 654-667).

Heavy use of `style={{ backgroundColor, borderColor, boxShadow }}` inline instead of Tamagui token props (`bg`, `borderColor`) — consistent with palette being passed as raw hex strings, which is why the static light palette leaks through; switching to theme tokens would also fix the dark-mode bug.
SelectionButton (step.tsx:1284-1287) deliberately avoids Tamagui Button to allow multi-line wrapping — a reasonable documented workaround, not a defect.
platform_notes: iPad: content IS width-constrained via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (step.tsx:434) rather than edge-to-edge, but it uses contentMaxWidth (~1040) rather than formMaxWidth (600), so a single-column form reads as a scaled-up phone layout on the large canvas.

No split-view / master-detail is attempted; for a strictly sequential 9-step wizard that is defensible, but the wide canvas could host the step-pill nav as a persistent left rail (the 9 steps already render as pills at step.tsx:669-703) turning this into a master-detail layout.

Native stack header is used (useYeeStackHeaderOptions, headerTitleAlign center on iOS); status bar and header render cleanly in the capture, no safe-area clipping. The footer adds bottomInset (step.tsx:1680 `paddingBottom: bottomInset + 12`) so the home-indicator area is handled.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios (estimated only); the dark/light palette mismatch is the structural issue rather than a specific failing pair.
Runtime states not shown: loading spinner, error NoticeCard, the 'If yes, rate the condition' follow-up, and saving spinner on Next.
Cross-step flow and how the footer/step-pill navigation behaves across the full 9 steps.
Whether the dark capture was generated with the dark preference actually set (the symptom strongly implies the screen ignores it, confirmed by the static import).
score_rationale: Usable with clear problems (5-6 band). The wizard is coherent, on-brand, and does constrain/center content, but it has a code-verified theme bug (renders light palette in the dark set via the static designSystem import) and a verified iPad layout miss (form column uses contentMaxWidth instead of formMaxWidth, plus no fontScale and a non-aligned full-width footer). These are concrete, fixable defects that keep it below the solid/minor-polish tier.
